title: Introduction to coloRify
text: 🌈 Colorify makes color creation modification intuitive effortless. Colorify lightweight dependency-free yet combines functionality popular color visualization packages, including: viridis palettes, perceptually uniform colorblind-friendly: Viridis, Turbo, Inferno, Cividis, Plasma, Rocket & Mako. Rcolorbrewer palettes inspired palette visualization. ggplot2 easy--use integration scale_color_* scale_fill_* bindings. base R (grDevices) palettes: Rainbow, Heat, Terrain, Topo, Cm & hcl/pal palettes. Okabe-Ito palette, highly distinct colorblind-safe scheme.

title: Introduction to coloRify
text: run coloRify, simply install package CRAN… …development version GitHub load library. Note coloRify uses hexcolors (e.g.: ‘#FF0000FF’) includes base R colors (e.g.: ‘red’) grDevices:

title: Introduction to coloRify
text: basic call just n(=10) colors requested. n takes integer > 0.  See output coloRify returns hexcolor vector.
code: colorify(n = 10, plot = TRUE) #>  [1] "#E974E6FF" "#EEB723FF" "#48EEFCFF" "#D341F1FF" "#A37515FF" "#84EF83FF" #>  [7] "#BBF963FF" "#221DE6FF" "#A77971FF" "#B38ED5FF"

title: Introduction to coloRify
text: show different seed yields different generated colors. Pass seed integer.
code: c <- colorify(10, plot = TRUE, seed = 1337)

title: Introduction to coloRify
text: can give custom colors generate rest, always enough colors plotting calls!
code: c <- colorify(colors = c("red", "white", "blue"), n = 5, plot = TRUE)

title: Introduction to coloRify
text: Set names output hexcolor vector. colors_names takes character vector names length amount requested colors.
code: c <- colorify(colors = c("red", "white", "blue"), n = 5, colors_names = paste0('name', rep(1:5)), plot = TRUE)

title: Introduction to coloRify
text: Order hexcolor output. Integer given starting point ordering, may negative.
code: # set integer for the ordering starting position c <- colorify(colors = c("red", "white", "blue"), n = 5, order = 2, plot = TRUE) c <- colorify(colors = c("red", "white", "blue"), n = 5, order = 3, plot = TRUE) # negative integer inverses the order  c <- colorify(colors = c("red", "white", "blue"), n = 5, order = -1, plot = TRUE)

title: Introduction to coloRify
text: Set transparency colors. alpha takes float ranging [0-1].
code: c <- colorify(colors = c("red", "white", "blue"), n = 5, alpha = .25, plot = TRUE)

title: Introduction to coloRify
text: can supply available palette colors, expanded requested n.
code: c <- colorify(colors = c("Okabe-Ito"), plot = TRUE) # note the 10th color is generated c <- colorify(colors = c("Okabe-Ito"), plot = TRUE, n = 10) # note that blue and yellow are cut, as only 10 colors are requested.  c <- colorify(colors = c("Okabe-Ito", "red", "blue", "yellow"), plot = TRUE, n = 10)

title: Introduction to coloRify
text: Easy color gradients using ‘nn’ parameter, also custom available palettes.
code: g1 <- colorify(colors = c("orange", "red", "white", "blue", "orange"), nn = 100, plot = TRUE) g2 <- colorify(colors = c("pastel2"), nn = 100, plot = TRUE)

title: Introduction to coloRify
text: Plot options, default circular output, plot = include ‘’ image ‘l’ plot color index labels.
code: g1 <- colorify(colors = c("orange", "red", "white", "blue", "orange"), nn = 15, plot = 'l') g1 <- colorify(colors = c("orange", "red", "white", "blue", "orange"), nn = 15, plot = 'i') g1 <- colorify(colors = c("orange", "red", "white", "blue", "orange"), nn = 15, plot = 'il')

title: Introduction to coloRify
text: Values factors, let’s say want palette less RGB (red, green, blue)/HSL (hue, saturation, lightness), can simply tweak specific channels! Values intuitively ranged [0-100] (instead 0-255). Factors multiplicative. order values factors called matters, play around combinations obtain ideal custom palettes. Note gradient made ‘n’ parameter , palettes actually called functions internally.
code: g3 <- colorify(100, colors = c("viridis"), plot = T) # r = red, f = factor: rf = 2 to multiply all red values  g4 <- colorify(100, colors = c("viridis"), rf = 2, plot = T) # v = value: rv = 50 to increase all red values by 50, on a scale between 0-100 g5 <- colorify(100, colors = c("viridis"), rv = 50, plot = T) # first, multiply red values by 2, then increase red values by 50 g6 <- colorify(100, colors = c("viridis"), rf = 2, rv = 50, plot = T) # first, increase red values by 50, then multiply red values by 2 g7 <- colorify(100, colors = c("viridis"), rv = 50, rf = 2, plot = T) # float factor decrease values by multiplication g8 <- colorify(100, colors = c("viridis"), bf = .5, plot = T) # negative values work to decrease values  g9 <- colorify(100, colors = c("viridis"), bv = -100, gv = -50, plot = T)

title: Introduction to coloRify
text: value factor adjustments made, .min .max parameters used set minimum maximum RGB/HSL values.
code: g3 <- colorify(100, colors = c("viridis"), plot = T) g8 <- colorify(100, colors = c("viridis"), bf = .5, plot = T) # same factor decrease, yet limited by minimum value g10 <- colorify(100, colors = c("viridis"), bf = .5, bmin = 40, plot = T) # need factor/value change to use min/max value  g11 <- colorify(100, colors = c("viridis"), bf = 1, bmax = 40, plot = T) # can use them in combination g12 <- colorify(100, colors = c("viridis"), bf = 1, bmin = 40, bmax = 40,  plot = T)

title: Introduction to coloRify
text: colors_lock can used locking specific colors numerical index, starting 1. colors_lock can also used patterning, long nn % length boolean character == 0. colors_lock can inversed putting ! front given vector.
code: c <- colorify(colors = c("pastel2"), nn = 30, plot = TRUE) # lock by index c <- colorify(colors = c("pastel2"), nn = 30, colors_lock = c(4,5,6, 10,11,12), lf = .5, plot = T) # inverse lock by index c <- colorify(colors = c("pastel2"), nn = 30, colors_lock = -c(4:12), lf = .5, plot = T) # lock by patterns c <- colorify(colors = c("pastel2"), nn = 30, colors_lock = c(TRUE, FALSE), lf = .5, plot = T) c <- colorify(colors = c("pastel2"), nn = 30, colors_lock = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE), lf = .5, plot = T)

title: Introduction to coloRify
text: colors_map takes vector values matching vector (generated) colors, returning color_map function can used generate colors based supplied values .
code: color_map <- colorify(colors = c('red', 'white', 'blue'), colors_map = c(0, 500, 1000)) # note the map is then given values to map back to the given color ranges from colors_map m1 <- colorify(colors = color_map(0:1000), plot = T)
